paper.title_en: Spinning-particle dynamics around Barrow’s nonlinear charged black hole
paper.abstract_en: In this work, we investigate the trajectories of spinning test particles in the gravitational background of Barrow’s nonlinear charged black hole, specified by a nonlinearity parameter <math altimg="si40.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1428"><mi>α</mi></math> and an electric charge <math altimg="si39.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1433"><mi>Q</mi></math>. The dynamics of the spinning particles are formulated within the framework of the Mathisson–Papapetrou–Dixon (MPD) equations, and the associated effective potential governing their motion is systematically derived. We examine the behavior of circular orbits and investigate the influence of the spin parameter <math altimg="si156.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1438"><mi>s</mi></math>, the black hole charge <math altimg="si39.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1444"><mi>Q</mi></math>, and the parameter <math altimg="si40.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1449"><mi>α</mi></math> on the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), the specific energy, and the angular momentum. Critical spin values <math altimg="si204.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1454"><msub><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext>max</mtext></mrow></msub></math> are identified, beyond which the particle’s motion becomes superluminal and thus non-physical. Furthermore, we compute the center-of-mass energy resulting from collisions of spinning particles near the black hole horizon. A key aspect of this work is the analysis of the deflection angle for spinning particles in the equatorial plane. By numerically solving the equations of motion, we demonstrate how spin and black hole parameters affect the bending of trajectories, offering new insights into the role of spin-curvature interaction in modified gravity spacetimes.
